d:
An experimental cancer vaccine has helped patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), an aggressive form of blood cancer, live a median of 24 months, compared with 14.7 months among those receiving other available treatments.
The Phase 3 REGAL trial involved 126 patients whose cancer had relapsed and who could not undergo a stem-cell transplant. The company behind the vaccine, SELLAS Life Sciences, reported a 41 per cent reduction in the risk of death among patients who received the vaccine.
